title: Governance: policy, ownership and the security review

videos.script: Twenty-four lessons built controls around one assistant. A company has more than one, and governance starts with knowing what exists. {{title}} The register names every system, its owner, its provider and its last review. Checked against the staff list, one owner has left. {{register}} Checked against the provider's bill, one system was never registered at all. The bill is the inventory nobody can forget. {{bill}} A change that adds reach gets a security review. What it adds decides what it must show. A refund tool needs a budget and a runbook. {{review}} And two names: the owner, and somebody who is not the author. {{approvals}} NIST's framework sorts the work into govern, map, measure and manage. ISO 42001 can be certified. Neither stops a prompt leaking a key. {{frameworks}} What does is a calendar, and controls that run on their own, say what they found, and exit with a status. {{end}}
